To solve this problem, we need to consider the concept of time dilation in special relativity. 

  From your perspective, as you travel at the speed of light, time appears to stand still for you. This is because time dilation occurs when an object moves at a significant fraction of the speed of light relative to an observer. In this case, since you're traveling at the speed of light, time dilation is extreme.

  From the child's perspective, however, time is passing normally. The child is still growing and aging at the same rate as if you were still on Earth.

  Since you traveled 5 light years to reach the child, you would experience time passing normally, but the child would experience time passing normally as well. 

  When you arrive, the child would be 5 years old from his perspective.
